author: lu_pinto
content:
sorry the delay in coming back to this. After reading through I have a feeling this is a bit of "patching" for this specific behaviour without having a more pragmatic approach.
Idea from my side, would like instead of partitioning the gas into execution and state at the start of the transaction, e.g. `execution_gas < TX_MAX_GAS_LIMIT` and being `state_gas` assigned the remainder, why not having a general unified pool `gas_left` and then have separate `execution_gas` budget for the frame (63/64th rule) but also check that the transaction cannot go over the `TX_MAX_GAS_LIMIT`. Maybe these are too many checks for the EVM at runtime but I'm failing to see a cleaner solution to this whole shebang.

author: lu_pinto
content: But I can see the security implications of the growth of `gas_left` at the child frame since assumptions about the `63/64th` rule is no longer an invariant one. You can get more gas for execution in the child frame above that limit. This might reintroduce problems that the `63/64th` rule tried to fix

author: misilva73
content: From what I can remember, the idea of the reservoir came from trying to keep gas observability still okay. If gas_left includes both regular and state gas, it could seem that if you still can spend more gas, but in fact you can't because part of that budget **can only** be used to state creation.

author: misilva73
content: I don't think we should change this at this point

author: lu_pinto
content: yeah I know I will get shot at this stage but just wanted to say it anyway 😂

author: lu_pinto
content:
I'm in favor of the change then, as without it, we are kind of opening a small breach in the 63/64th rule from what I can see.
I would have liked the design to have gone a different way since my gut feeling tells me that yet another edge case will follow, but it could be just me.
